summary: ps-bool ships only an obfuscated exec payload that runs on import
details: The sole module shipped in both the sdist and the wheel, main.py, consists entirely of `exec(zlib.decompress(base64.b85decode('...')))` at the top level. The package exposes this module as `py_modules=['main']` and wires it as the `psbool` console_script, so the opaque, compressed-and-encoded blob is decoded and executed unconditionally the first time the module is imported or the CLI is invoked. There is no source, documentation, or API surface — the entire implementation is a single encoded payload, deliberately concealing its behavior from anyone inspecting the package before it runs. A boolean-logic utility has no legitimate reason to ship its implementation as an opaque exec-of-decoded-bytes blob; this is the canonical obfuscated-payload import-time execution shape and causes an arbitrary author-controlled program to run on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
